articleTitle: Robust Dual-Current Control of a Three-Phase Grid-Tied Inverter under Unbalanced Grid Voltage Using LMI Approach
abstract: In this paper, a robust dual-current control is proposed for a three-phase grid-tied inverter under unbalanced grid voltage. To compensate the unbalanced grid current rooted by the grid voltage dips or faults, an additional negative sequence compensator is considered in this proposed controller. The current control for both positive and negative sequence utilizes state feedback with integral control to archive fast reference tracking without steady-state error. The robust control gain is computed by solving a linear matrix inequality-based optimization problem to obtain fast convergence rate in the presence of the uncertainty of the system. The positive sequence current reference is used to regulate the amount of current flow from DC source to the grid, and the zero negative sequence reference is used to compensate the unbalanced grid current. To verify the efficacy of this control method, a comparison between the proposed robust dual-current control and robust current control without negative sequence compensator is conducted using simulation.

articleTitle: Design of a Robust Control for a Single-Phase AC-DC Converter Using LMI Technique
abstract: The dq-synchronous frame method is a widely used framework for three-phase converters due to its DC like character. However, a single-phase wave form cannot be converted directly into a dq-signal. Thus, this proposed controller utilizes all-pass filters to create imaginary B-signals from the original AC voltage and current. Then, aB-signals can be simply converted into dq-signals using the transform matrix. This proposed controller consists of a double loops control, robust inner loop, and outer loop PI control. The robust control uses state feedback with integral control to eliminate steady state error and bring stability to the system. The gains of controller determine by solving optimization problem so that the convergence time is minimize with the presence of uncertainty of the L-filter. The simulation studies are conducted to verify the efficiency of the proposed method using PSIM simulation tool.

articleTitle: Ripeness Classification of a Bunch of Bananas Using a CNN
abstract: Bananas are one of the richest sources of vitamins and minerals in the world and bananas are also one of Thailand's most economically significant fruit crops. Images of a bunch of bananas were used to train a Convolution Neural Network (CNN). The convolutional layers applied different filters as feature detectors to create a feature map representing the detected input features. Then the features were shaped into one-dimensional features and sent to an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) for the banana ripeness classification. The results showed that the classification was quite accurate. Using the same set of images for both training and testing, the CNN achieved the accuracy of 100.00%. The average classification accuracy of 91.21% was achieved when testing with images excluded from training. The classification accuracy from class 0 to class 4 was 93.94%, 90.00%, 87.50%, 89.47% and 92.31%, respectively.

articleTitle: Haar-CNN Cascade for Facial Expression Recognition
abstract: Recognizing emotions can aid in the interpretation and communication of non-verbal communication. Although deep neural networks perform well in automatically extracting and learning high-level representations of facial features from large amounts of multidimensional data, there is still a need for a face detection model to work fast for real-time applications. This working experiment investigates the use of Haar features as another feature extraction stage for a deep neural network to decrease the dimensionality of inputs in facial detection prior to expression recognition which is applied to multi-scale facial expression recognition (FER). Hybrid approaches are used for locating and categorizing facial features, with the initial approach consisting of Haar feature extraction combined with CNN-based models. The proposed inclusion of Haar Cascade with CNN demonstrated a recognition rate exceeding 90% for all facial expressions, with the greatest accuracy achieved in identifying “Happy” and “Surprise” expressions.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Pulse Shape Analysis for Progression of Insulation Degradation in Medium Voltage Cable
abstract: Measurement of partial discharge (PD) pulses is a method used in quantifying PD activity within defective insulation. PD pulses propagate away from the defect along the cable and can be measured by sensors such as high frequency current transformers (HFCT). These PD pulses contain information that describes the behavior of PD activity in the degrading insulation. Pulse shape analysis (PSA) is an efficient method to analyze the degradation behavior of insulation. In this study, the PSA is performed on a medium voltage cable sample with surface discharges emerging from a damaged cable termination. PSA is performed based on rise time, fall time, and pulse width of individual PD pulses that are extracted from the PD data measured in the form of phase resolved PD pattern under increasing electrical stress conditions. The Gaussian model is implemented to find best-fit lines which describe the correlation of PSA quantities and electrical stress. The presented study results can be useful in improving the diagnostics of aging power cables.

articleTitle: Money Management for Trading Strategies
abstract: Investors generally focus primarily on trading algorithms and not on money management, causing their portfolios to be seriously damaged when things go wrong. In this research, various methods of money management are presented. Along with presenting the equation used to describe the growth of the investment portfolio. So that investors can design trading strategies more efficiently.

articleTitle: Short-term Load Demand Forecasting using Supervised Deep Learning Techniques: A Case Study of Suranaree University of Technology
abstract: The implementation of effective energy management necessitates the accurate forecasting of load demand. This study presents the efficacy and accuracy of supervised deep learning in forecasting short-term load demand. The deep learning technique is a neural network-based machine learning widely applied for load demand forecasting tasks. This study utilized five deep learning techniques: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units (BiGRU), CNN-GRU, and CNN-BiGRU. The daily electricity load demand data from the Suranaree University of Technology, Nakhon Ratchasima Province, Thailand, from January 1, 2022, to August 28, 2022, and the average daily temperature from NASA's data source were used to train the proposed deep learning techniques and forecast three-day load demand. By comparing the CNN, GRU, CNN-GRU, and CNN-BiGRU techniques, the BiGRU technique provides the most accurate three-day load demand forecast. The respective MAE, MAPE, and RMSE error indices are 20.38kW, 1.99%, and 30.3kW, respectively. The study's results demonstrate the effectiveness of deep learning techniques for forecasting short-term load demand.

articleTitle: Ad-hoc Aerial-view Vehicle Detection and Tracking for Real-Time Traffic Monitoring Using YOLOv7
abstract: We have proposed an aerial view vehicle detection, classification, and tracking system using the You Look Only Once Version 7 (YOLOv7) machine learning model for automatic ad-hoc traffic statistical information gathering. The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) flies and gathers real-time visual data in areas where stationary cameras are unavailable such as rural roads or highway traffics. Eight different types of vehicles are detected and classified followed by tracking. Statistical data such as flow rate, direction, and car density are obtained afterward. The overall accuracy for the classification part is 93%, while the individual accuracies go as high as 99.5% for some classes.

articleTitle: Improved Fuzzy C-means Clustering for Grape Leaf Disease Detection using Mathematical Morphology
abstract: Grapevines may show various symptoms that negatively affect the vigor and production of the grapes. In this study, the classification of diseases was performed by identifying the distinctive features of grape leaf lesions on digital photographs to facilitate treatment and control of the symptoms of the disease from an early stage. A set of 5,700 images of grape leaves consisting of 1,500 images of downy mildew-infected grape leaves, 1,400 images of rust-infected grape leaves, 1,600 images of Anthracnose-infected leaves and 1,200 images of healthy leaves was used. Pre-processing procedures included 1) Image Sharpening using Laplacian Filters to enhance or improve the details in the images by reducing blur and enhancing the edges. 2) Gray Scale Image to convert the image into a white and black gradient (Halftone Image). 3) Noise Reduction using Smoothing Spatial Filters to reduce the noise based on blurring effect such as reducing fine details or connecting gaps in straight lines or curves. 4) Fuzzy C-means Clustering (FCMC), an algorithm that allows overlapping or redundancy of data in each cluster through the determination of membership degree of each cluster. This clustering method is widely used in fields such as medicine, science and engineering. 5) Mathematical Morphology, the comparison of characteristics and appearance of grape leaf lesions. The results showed that, from 5,700 images, the average accuracy of disease classification for downy mildew, rust, anthracnose and healthy leaves was 96.7742%, 97.9871%, 95.3877% and 96.7742%, respectively. The results obtained can be used for further development and applications in agriculture.

articleTitle: Inventory Management System based on IoT and Microservices Architecture Design
abstract: This paper presents the inventory management system based on IoT and microservices architecture that synced between IoT (Internet of Things) and web application. There are two main parts consisting of IoT forklift vehicle and data transmitted system by MQTT protocol. Microservice can utilize data to process business logic and provides API. Inventory area includes a zone, a subzone and parking area for forklifts to scan QR code on each subzone. Data of forklifts is published to back-end service. The results of system microservice publish information events and processes business data to the admin client with a delay under a second.

articleTitle: Capacitively-Loaded Spiral Array based RF Metasurfaces for Boosting the Performance of 1.5T MRI
abstract: The narrow-band resonance in metamaterial is exploited in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to facilitate boosting of magnetic field and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). However, most of the reported metamaterials for 1. 5T MRI applications focus on three-dimensional structures, which are unsuitable for practical implementations since they are electrically large and bulky. Here, we demonstrate a spiral-array based ultra-thin metasurface, which can be used as an ‘add-on’ for enhancing the performance of 1. 5 T MRI. The metasurface is integrated with phantom and bio-model mimicking human properties to enhance the magnetic field inside the region-of-interest (ROI) of specimens undergoing scan. Inductive coupling between these capacitively-loaded closely spaced spirals causes an enhancement of the signal-to-noise ratio by ~3. 5 times for 1. 5T MRI while maintaining the specific absorption ratio (SAR) well below the safety limit. The proposed structure can be easily integrated in the available tight space (of thickness ≤ 2 mm) of clinical MRI scanners where the placement of any bulky additional structure is challenging.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of MPPT for PV Systems using ANFIS Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes designing and simulating a PV power generation system with maximum power point tracking using an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) algorithm. ANFIS combines neural networks and fuzzy logic principles, potentially capturing both benefits in a single algorithm. Characteristics and parameters of a 255 Wp PV panel(Advance Power API-P2555) were used to simulate using the conditions as the panel temperature of 25 oC and the solar irradiance of 1000 W/m<sup>2</sup>, 500 W/m<sup>2</sup>, and 100 W/m<sup>2</sup>, respectively. The simulation results showed that when the system connects to the MPPT using the ANFIS model, then the system can produce the maximum output power in all case studies.

articleTitle: Compact Diplexer Based on Stub-loaded Dual-mode Resonator
abstract: A compact diplexer based on stub loaded dual-mode resonator is presented in this paper. The optimized T-junction microstrip line combines two independent dual-mode resonator filters. This dual-mode configuration is easily controllable resonant modes and transmission zero position, improving the filter and diplexer frequency response. The fabricated diplexer with the lower and upper resonant frequencies at 1.95 GHz and 2.14 GHz is designed to verify the proposed configuration. The proposed diplexer has isolation better than 21 dB, and insertions are better than 1.1 dB in both channels.

articleTitle: Stability investigation of two distributed generation in DC microgrids
abstract: In this paper, an investigation of stability of the decentralized DC microgrid is presented. The studied system consists of two distributed generations (DGs) connected to the load via long cables. A DC-DC boost converter is considered for DGs and a load. The boost converters are functioned in a continuous-conduction mode (CCM). Two cases are studied. In case 1, PI controller is utilized to control the boost converters. In case 2, due to passivity definition, each DG is controlled using passivity-based control. For the current sharing between DGs, the droop voltage control is applied in two cases. The simulation results using MATLAB/Simulink software are presented for both cases.

articleTitle: A Study on GCN using Focal Loss on Class-Imbalanced Bitcoin Transaction for Anti-Money Laundering Detection
abstract: Due to a complexity of Bitcoin transaction graph and a class-imbalance difficulty as only a few known labels of blockchain illicit activities exist, graph convolutional network (GCN) using focal loss constraints is applied in this paper for anti-money laundering detection. The GCN, composed of spectral graph convolution layers suitably handles graph structured input data; whereas the focal loss (FL) has been applied to resolve the severe problem of class-imbalance by reducing the loss weight of easy-to-classify samples. In addition, the licit and illicit detection performance comparison on Elliptic dataset among 2, 4 and 6 numbers of GCN layer (GCN -2L, -4L and -6L) relying upon focal loss relative to cross-entropy (CE) loss is assessed. Assessment criteria depend on precision, recall, F1 and accuracy scores, averaged through 10-fold cross validation. A Bitcoin transaction graph, so-called Elliptic dataset derived from Bitcoin blockchain is experimented to detect illicit transactions. The results indicate insignificant difference of accuracy rate between GCN -2L, -4L and -6L models using FL and those employing CE. However, apparently and interestingly, illicit transactions are 4.78%, 5% and 6.20% more correctly predicted by using FL than CE, consecutively relying on GCN -2L, 4L and 6L. Illicit transactions are 4.94%, 5.31% and 7.84% less misclassified by FL than CE.

articleTitle: Axial Ratio Enhancing in Perfect Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna
abstract: Three-dimensional axial ratio plots of several known circularly polarized microstrip antennas are discussed. We have found that the accepted AR value for CP wave (AR!3dB) for these antennas does not occur at the desired radiation pattern range. We then propose a perfect CP radiation microstrip antenna, where CP wave radiates covering the front of the antenna. The results show the agreement of operating frequency, AR bandwidth, gain and radiation pattern. Furthermore, the absolute electrical field direction at different observation time steps also supports the perfect CP rotation.

articleTitle: Comparison of Feature Extraction Methods for Classifying Energy Theft and Defective Meters in Automatic Meter Reading
abstract: Loss is an important factor for any organization that operates in the distribution of electric power. Non-Technical Loss (NTL) is one of the challenging losses. Most distributors attempt to find a way to reduce the NTL loss. In some cases, the anomaly patterns are complex, similar, and difficult to classify. This paper proposes a feature extraction method using signal modeling methods obtained from voltage and current in a 3-phase system for abnormalities in the Automatic Meter Reading (AMR) of the Provincial Electricity Authority (PEA). Focusing on the main causes of NTL include energy theft and defective meters using supervised learning for classification. All-pole modeling has been applied to extract the feature as a coefficient. The voltage and current load profiles are divided into 1-week intervals (672 values) and fed into the signal modeling to be extracted as 4 coefficients. The methods can reduce the number of features before input into the model, which makes the model process faster and improves performance. The experimental results show that extraction using Prony's method and k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN) model significantly outperforms other methods.

articleTitle: Investigating the applicable position of established cloud servers using the hybrid partitional clustering
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid partition clustering, which is the combination of three techniques: partitional clustering, proportional allocation, and center-of-gravity. The objective of this hybrid clustering is to identify the applicable position of established cloud servers to support the testing of a high-speed internet platform. These cloud servers will be installed in the Eastern region of Thailand. Moreover, hybrid clustering is developed using RStudio and R packages. The latitude-longitude position and the number of populations from each district that has internet service providers are considered as main factors to do the cluster. Regarding the experiment, we found that K-Means provide a better solution than K-Medoid with a silhouette width value equal to 0.45. In addition, the results of this hybrid clustering will also be compared with the existing solution. The difference in sample users between these two methods is approximately 25 percent.

articleTitle: Dual-band UHF and HF-RFID Tag Antenna for Tracking and Energy Harvesting Applications
abstract: This paper proposed the dual-band (UHF and HF) RFID tag antenna operating in the frequency bands of 920–925 MHz and 13.56 MHz for tracking and energy harvesting applications. The tag antenna consists of two parts of a patch dipole antenna for electromagnetic radiation in the UHF band and a spiral antenna for magnetic-field emission in the HF band. From the simulated results, the proposed antenna with an appropriate arrangement can provide the antenna impedance compatible with the RFID chips in both frequency bands. The measured results show that the prototype tag antenna can communicate with the maximum read range in both frequency bands and can harvest energy in the HF band.

articleTitle: Design of Vivaldi Array Antenna for Hydrogen Line Observation and Weather Radar Application
abstract: A low cost and low profile <tex>$2\times 2$</tex> Vivaldi array antenna is designed and developed to observe and detect the 1.42 GHz hydrogen line emission from the space. Firstly, the single element of Vivaldi antenna is designed at operating frequency of 1.42 GHz which obtains the directional pattern with the average gain around 4 dBi. To achieve high gain and decrease HPBW, the <tex>$2\times 2$</tex> Vivaldi array antenna is introduced and each element receives signal through 1 to 4 Wilkinson power divider. The proposed array antenna obtains 60 deg-HPBW with low side lobe level. Moreover, the average gain is around 9.5 dBi for measurement with the clear properties of linear polarization. Finally, the proposed Vivaldi array antenna is going to apply and employ as receiver for hydrogen line spectrum and also weather radar application.

articleTitle: Coordinated-axis Weight for Real-Time Trace Transform
abstract: This paper presents a method for building Coordinated-axis Weight (CW) that has the advantage can be used to increase the speed for converting image data into the domain of real-time trace transforms. The main idea for this method is to use a feature reduction method for image data that must be used in cooperation with supervised machine learning outcome predictions. But the obtained result still retains the distinctive features of the data image in the form of a trace transform. Start by reducing the number of features from the image data, which will be used to reduce the size of the image to the appropriate image size, which in this article will reduce the image size to 45x45 pixels. The next step is to train the data using a Decision Tree (DT) method by aligning the reduced image data in a 1D model. In addition to the image data, two more features are added, i.e. the <tex>$\phi$</tex> and <tex>$\rho$</tex> positions, to inform the prediction that each position has a different value. And the last step is to bring the data to create a model for predicting the answer. The weights obtained from the model are called Coordinated-axis Weights (CW). The experiments within this paper were experimented using the Caltech-256 database, which was able to measure the MSE, RMSE, and PNSR of the images compared to the original trace transform response images at 4.1, 2.02, and 42.00, respectively, including the highest predictive speed of 0.2 ms per image.

articleTitle: A Novel Determination of Soluble NPK Nutrient Measurement System Using K-means and SOM Methods Compared with UV Visible Spectrophotometer
abstract: Technologies are currently being used in smart farms to improve productivity. Agricultural innovation is also widespread. Therefore, the development of Internet of Things (IoTs) technologies and devices to collect data is important. Finding essential nutrients for growth such as Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P) and Potassium (K) are important factors. Competitiveness is the important key for growing vertically or indoors. However, soil testing can be expensive, complicated and time consuming. The development of devices that can effectively measure nutrient NPK levels could be used over time. This paper presents a suitable clustering using the K-means method and a forecasting method using the Self-Organizing Map (SOM) method to enhance the device's ability to analyze nutrients in real time. A total of 50,688 samples were tested using the K-Means clustering algorithm, and the sample data were also analyzed. A SOM was prepared to predict the accuracy of the analysis. A total of 11,486 samples were tested and analyzed, then the results of the soluble NPK nutrient monitoring system were taken. It has an efficiency of 84.15% compared to using a UV Visible spectrophotometer, allowing data to be predicted during nutrient solubility changes and to operate according to the proposed system. Therefore, the unsupervised machine learning will improve the measurement system of future cultivation systems.

articleTitle: Distributions of Flux and Electromagnetic Force in Brushless Motor Using 3-D FEM
abstract: This paper presents a mathematical model of the electromagnetic field. and the electromagnetic force of a DC brushless electric motor. The 3-D finite element method (3-D FEM) was applied to analyze the electromagnetic field. and electromagnetic forces in the design of DC brushless electric motors. In this research, the design of a three-phase, four-pole, 3-hp DC brushless electric motor is considered in two forms: 6 permanent magnets and 10 permanent magnets, but the magnetic properties and parameters. remain the same, and the results shown are the values of the magnetic field distributed along the motor cross-sectional area. This is explained by a graphical representation of the magnetic field distribution. To determine the electromagnetic load of a brushless motor in an analysis of the ideal DC brushless motor design.

articleTitle: Deployment of Machine Vision Platform for Checking Spot Welds on Metal Strap Belts
abstract: This paper presents a designed platform used to detect the perfection and number of spot welds on the strap belt of metal sheet coils. Three different approaches include image morphology, thresholding and Hough transform are compared. The results from real implementation show that using the adaptive threshold values in image thresholding approach instead of fixed value can increase the system accuracy from 69% to 88%. Also, to find the pad, the comparison of using Haar cascade machine learning and YOLO deep learning is described.

articleTitle: A Single-Phase Integrated Battery Charger Simulation Compare On-board Battery Charger with PFC Boost Converter and PSFB DC-DC Converter
abstract: Currently, electrical vehicles (EVs) are popularly used, and various technologies have been developed to improve systems related to EVs. Electric vehicle charging systems will play an important role. The development of electric vehicle charging systems, one of the systems used to charge the battery of an electric vehicle for a single-phase system that can be used at home is a charging system consisting of a power factor collector (PFC) boost converter in combination with a Phase-Shift Full-Bridge (PSFB) dc-dc converter. There is one charging system has been developed that can be charged directly through the coil wiring of an electric vehicle's electric machine for reducing device usage semiconductors used in the charging circuit and including being able to increase the space for the EVs. In this paper present a simulation of two types of battery charging systems, one is an electric vehicle charging system that uses a PFC circuit combined with a PSFB that uses an LLC resonant converter and IBC system to compare the operation to charge the batteries of both systems using MATLAB Simulink software for a 48 V 150 Ah lithium-ion battery. As a result, the state of charge (SOC) of the battery increases during both charging systems, thereby confirming the suitability of the charging system. The battery in electric vehicles uses the IBC system to develop converters for use in energy storage systems.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Standard LQG and Minimax LQG for Speed Control of Induction Motors
abstract: This paper presents the application of the minimax linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) controller design for induction motor speed control with uncertain noise. Comparative studies show that the controller designed via the minimax LQG method performs better response than the standard LQG design in terms of disturbance rejection and reference speed tracking.

articleTitle: Utilisation of Solar Rooftops for Energy Reduction: a case study for Airport Rail Link
abstract: This paper proposes the solution to energy reduction in a traction railway power supply system using solar PV rooftop installations at train stations. The train operation and energy consumption are simulated in MATLAB program using a case study of the Airport Rail Link (ARL) commuter line in Bangkok, Thailand. The station roof areas are estimated from the satellite view of Google Map. The result shows that a 28 percent reduction in daily traction energy consumption can be achieved, regardless of the power losses in the catenary system and traction substation. Therefore, the energy cost from the grid is also reduced. This considerable amount of the saved energy is worth considering feasibility study in terms of return on investment.

articleTitle: Influence of Wind Direction on the Ion Flow Field of 500kV HVDC Lines
abstract: An important aspect in the HVDC transmission lines is the ion flow field at the ground level. The ion flow field of ±500 kV HVDC double circuits with the dedicated metallic return conductors is presented in this paper. We aim to clarify the effect of transverse wind direction on the electric field on the ground and the ion current density. The transmission lines are simulated by using the upwind finite volume method (FVM). The influence of wind direction from positive to negative conductors yields higher current density and electric field peaks than that in the opposite direction. The ground-level electric field is similar for both wind directions. The peak positions of current density on the ground are close to the center line under the wind from the positive to the negative conductors. The opposite wind has the current peak near the right of way. Compared with the typical HVAC line, the HVDC lines have lower electric field at the peak position but higher field at the edge of right of way.

articleTitle: A New Unit Commitment Method of Large-scale Power Systems Based on Scenario Trees
abstract: The existing unit commitment (UC) methods require additional processes to handle minimum up- and down-time (MUT and MDT) constraints and hiddenly underestimate the historical operating data of the IEEE 10-unit test system, thus necessitating a computational burden for solving large-scale UC problems. For this reason, this paper proposes a new UC method based on scenario tree pre-construction to eliminate the MUT and MDT constraints. In addition, the operational data from the literature are used to provide a fast solution for optimal economic dispatch, leading to a data-driven approach. Different simulation cases reveal that our proposed method can replicate the same computation procedure of the IEEE 10-unit test system to efficiently solve IEEE 20- to 4000-unit test systems while maintaining the computational performance. Therefore, this method can effectively solve a large-scale UC within a short execution time. Numerical results have shown the superiority of our proposed approach as compared to the literature.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Infrastructure as a Service across Cloud Service Providers
abstract: The purpose of this research aims to monitor, analyze, and compare the performance of infrastructure as a service (IaaS) between the selective cloud providers. To assure which cloud provider has more stability, reliability, and scalability. This paper focuses on performance testing based on a deployed web server in the cloud environment. The main feature of cloud computing is scalability thus most common IaaS cloud service providers (CSPs) have Auto Scaling features for instances or virtual machines. Not only does this paper gives the experimental results of the scaling scalability testing, but it also provides the results of recovery testing to inspect how long a web server is able to recover from failures and load testing which simulated traffic requests. Testing was conducted in the major public clouds of Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Microsoft Azure, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). Azure performs the most efficiently of almost all testing but hardest to configure.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field Simulation of Pantograph for Electric Train Using 3D Finite Element Method
abstract: This paper presents a mathematical model of the magnetic field in a pantograph for an electric train. This is shown in the form of a partial differential equation. Second, the computer simulation applied the three-dimensional finite element method (3-D FEM) developed by the MATLAB program and analyzed the material that can be used as a replacement for pantograph contact surfaces. In this research, a voltage of 25 kV and a frequency of 50 Hz were used to simulate the contact effect of a pantograph. There are compare 4 comparable materials in total: copper, aluminum, brass, and carbon steel. To find materials with electromagnetic diffusion to replace graphite materials.

articleTitle: Tire Pressure Monitoring System Using Low-Frequency RFID Energy Harvesting
abstract: In this paper, we deploy the RFID technology for a tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS). RFID has the distinguishing feature for transmitting power wirelessly to a TPMS device. This enables the TPMS system to work battery-less and overcome the disadvantages associated with batteries. Our proposed system receives power from a low-frequency 134.2 kHz transmitter and stores it in a capacitor to enable the TPMS transponder. This power can successfully operate and transmit data from the sensor through the ultra-high-frequency 433 MHz to a reader installed inside the vehicle. The experimental results showed that it took only 34 seconds to charge the power when the reader distance was 6 cm, and the speed was 100 km/h.

articleTitle: Location, orientation, and speed tracking of a robot using ROS: a case study with Whycon
abstract: In this paper, a system that can track the absolute position, orientation, and speed of a single mobile robot was developed using ROS and the WhyCon localization algorithm. ROS nodes that receive WhyCon coordinates and return the orientation and speed of a mobile robot were developed. On-site experiments verify the accuracy of the system. Percent error of the computed position was found to be 6.67%, with orientation error at 0.612%, and speed error at 3.68%. The system can be used in a mobile robot testing facility.

articleTitle: Image processing technique for electrical characterization of red blood cells by electrorotation
abstract: Electrorotation (ROT) is one of cell electrical characterization techniques by observing the rotation of cells under a rotating electric field at different frequencies. Therefore, the accurate rotation rate is essential for determining cell characteristics. This work presents the method to determine the rotation rate by image processing techniques. Two features of the rotating cell were used to improve the accuracy of the method. In the experiment, the rotation rate of normal red blood cell was determined from its ROT video. It was found that the calculated rotation rate was consistent with the theory based on the single-shell model. These results showed that the developed method was adequately effective for the rotation rate analysis, and could reduce the processing time.

articleTitle: Development of monitoring PM2.5 based on IoT and Google Data Studio
abstract: This paper proposed the design and implementation of monitoring PM2.5 based on the IoT system using ESP8266, available data on Google Data Studio, an IoT system for monitoring and alerting PM2.5 dust. The system consists of ESP8266, PM2.5 sensor, temperature, relative humidity, and CO sensor. The results showed that the measurement of PM2.5 dust, the difference in PM2.5 dust measurements were 39.06, 26.56, 23.43, 14.06, 13.95, and 12.72 μg/m3. The measurement results are transferred to Google Sheets. For the storage of PM2.5, measurements were 4–11 μg/m3. The relative temperature and humidity measurements were 33, 40, 40, 36, 35, and 34 °C, and the humidity is related to the same trend. The CO measurement results were 120, 132, 123, 142, 162, and 140 ppm, and the average was 136.5 ppm. Test results and compare trends in the same direction. Additional research findings on the installation site determine the PM2.5 dust reduction plan for the next winter and dry season.

articleTitle: Estimation of Vertical Jump Height using Capacitive Sensing Method
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost vertical jump height measuring device based on the time-of-flight technique. A capacitive mat was developed and used as a sensing element to sense the athlete's feet. The capacitive mat was made from aluminum foils that dimensions of the capacitive mat ware with a width of 50.3 cm x length of 70.6 cm. The signal conditioning circuitry that was used as an analog front-end for measuring the capacitive was also described. The time difference between when athletes jumped off and reached the ground was calculated by a microcontroller. The jump height was recorded and stored via the computer. A total of 27 athletes, weighted between 48 kg to 115 kg were used as a sample. The testing results have shown that the proposed system has a percentage difference of 18.16%.

articleTitle: Electrical Discharge Plasma for Seed Priming of Green Oak Lettuce (Lactuca sativa)
abstract: This paper evaluates the use of gliding-arc plasma priming compared to hydropriming and osmopriming for enhancing the germination of green oak seeds. The results showed that plasma priming is an effective method for improving the germination of green oak seeds without causing harm, and it resulted in the most uniform and consistent germination. The average germination of all treated seeds is 80%, proving that neither direct plasma priming nor indirect plasma priming hinders the germination of green oak seeds. On the other hand, plasma treatment was also found to accelerate the germination of green oak seeds compared to other techniques. They provide the highest levels of uniform germination, taking only ~5 hours for 25-75% of the total number of seeds to germinate. The average germination time for seeds treated with direct and indirect plasma priming is faster than in other conditions. Specifically, it takes around 50 hrs compared to ~ 60 hrs for control, hydropriming, and osmopriming treatments. The germination-promoting effects of plasma treatment are likely due to the interaction of ions and free radicals with the seed surface, leading to surface modification and potentially acting as signaling molecules during germination. Overall, this study suggests that plasma priming is a promising approach for enhancing the germination of green oak seeds.

articleTitle: Piezoelectric Energy Harvester for a GPS Device Embedded in Hiking Shoes
abstract: This paper presents an experiment to find a suitable model for energy from a piezoelectric energy harvesting device attached to a sole. The experiment selected a model from 3 models to compare energy harvesting and find a model that harvests enough energy for a GPS device embedded in hiking shoes. The model with the shortest harvest time was selected. The piezoelectric used in the experiment was a Piezo Elements Buzzer Sounder Sensor which was stacked in 4 layers called the Piezo Elements Buzzer Sounder Sensor in a stack that was connected in parallel. The 3 models used in the experiment were to the stack of the sole in 3 different forms as follows: 1. Sole with a piezoelectric device attached in with 2 positions, 2-points in the metatarsal area, 2-points in the heel, and 4 layers per point; 2. Sole with a piezoelectric device attached in 1 position, 2-points in the heel, and 4 layers per point; 3. Sole with a piezoelectric device attached in one position, 2-points in the metatarsal, and 4 layers per point. From the experimental results, it was found that the model of a stack attached to the sole required the least amount of time to harvest energy in one charging charge which was completed in 87 seconds. This model used 2-points in the metatarsal area, 2- points in the heel, and 4 layers per point. Then EH300 was used to harvest energy and it was enough to supply a GPS device embedded in hiking shoes. EH300 took about 15 minutes to supply cycle of supply.

articleTitle: BIST Design and Implementation for a Fixed-Point Arithmetic MAC Unit within a Systolic Array
abstract: In embedded systems involving hardware accelerators to support embedded machine learning (ML) applications, both sequential and parallel operations are used to ensure the system can perform its required operations in the required time. For ML applications involving trained ML model inference, parallel (concurrent) hardware structures can be utilized to perform parallel multiplications usually involving matrix multiplication operations in hardware rather than software. In this paper, fault simulation, embedded instrument test access and built-in self-test (BIST) are considered in relation to the multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit that would be found within a systolic array. A fault simulation was performed on the pre-synthesis MAC unit Verilog HDL design module and used to develop a BIST unit accessible via an IEEE Std 1687 network. The design was prototyped using a Xilinx Artix-7 field programmable gate array (FPGA).

articleTitle: Weekly Load Demand Forecasting using Supervised Deep Learning Techniques: A Case Study of Suranaree University of Technology
abstract: This paper presents supervised deep learning techniques for weekly electrical load demand forecasting at the Suranaree University of Technology, Nakhon Ratchasima, Thailand. Deep learning is a modern artificial intelligent technique developed from neural networks-based machine learning that mimics the nervous system of living organisms. Six supervised deep learning techniques, i.e., Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) techniques, were used in this study. The supervised deep learning model was trained by daily load demand data from January 1, 2018, to May 18, 2022, before forecasting weekly load demand. The forecasting results show that LSTM, BiLSTM, and GRU are all techniques with minor errors. The BiLSTM technique, on the other hand, produced the most accurate forecasts, with an MAE of 13.07 kW, MAPE of 1.66%, and RMSE of 19.826 kW, respectively.

articleTitle: Detection of Magnetite Rust Using Circular Microstrip Patch Antenna-based Chipless RFID Sensor
abstract: In this paper, detection of the magnetite rust is presented by using a chipless RFID sensor based on a circular microstrip patch antenna (CMPA). The sensor is designed at the resonant frequency of 4.89 GHz by using a single-layer PCB with its dielectric constant of 4.3. Simulations were conducted to verify that the designed sensor can detect the magnetite rust through shifted resonant frequency. In simulations, the sensor was mounted on the iron with its magnetite rust. The width and depth of iron rust were varied in order to investigate the effect of iron rust on the resonant frequency. Simulation results have been shown that the proposed chipless RFID sensor and RCS’ can be utilized to detect the effect of the iron rust.

articleTitle: A CCII-Based Electrocardiogram Amplifier with DC Suppression
abstract: This paper presents the design of a CCII-based electrocardiogram (ECG) amplifier for ECG measurement using two second generation current conveyors (CCII) and five passive devices. An ECG amplifier is proposed in term of compact circuit and DC suppression for ECG measurement. The proposed circuit has the ability to suppress DC and out of band high frequency interference. The proposed circuit was simulated using a commercially available current conveyors AD844 and tested by PSPICE program. The simulation results show that the proposed amplifier attains a mid-band gain of 46 dB, Common Mode Rejection Ratio (CMRR) of 57.76 dB at 10 Hz, and input referred noise is 1.62 μVrms and the dynamic range is 66.78 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: A Non-contact Microwave Sensor System for Characterizing a Binary-liquid Mixed Concentration
abstract: This research presents a design and analysis of an open-loop microstrip resonator which is integrated with a microwave sensor system. It is used for measuring a binary-liquid mixed concentration of sodium chloride (NaCl) and DI-water to detect salinity level. The open-loop resonator is designed to provide a band-stop bandwidth of 1 GHz, which has operated from 2 GHz to 3 GHz. The proposed microwave sensor system consists of a microwave synthesizer, a voltage detector, and an open-loop resonator that is designed to operate at 3 GHz to characterize the salinity level of the sample liquid mixture. A liquid mixture samples of NaCl and Distill-water with 5 different concentration levels of 0%, 2%, 5%, 10%, and 20% were used to assess the salinity level for the proposed microwave sensor system.

articleTitle: Ischemic Stroke Post-treatment Prediction using Machine Learning to develop Web Application for Healthcare Centers in Thailand
abstract: Stroke attack is one of the most serious concerns in an emergency room. Expert diagnosis and accurate treatment are crucial for the improvement, death, or impairment of the patients. This work aims at using big data analytics for developing a system to provide the probability for each patient whether he would improve after medications. Records of N=1700 volunteers were gathered for non-linear classification training. Random Forest outperforms seven other methods compared in this study. The AI model was deployed as a web application for a rural hospital to assist medical personnel. This can be considered an important step towards AI-assisted emergency medications for stroke. Under the situation where the NIH Stroke Score was unavailable on time, the system could still provide the improvement probability via a web application based on the AI model trained in this work.

articleTitle: A Double Layer Interdigital CPW Metamaterial Director for LTE Antenna System
abstract: This paper proposes the design of metamaterial director for antenna, which has the feature of double layer based on CPW structure by using interdigital CPW technique. The designed unit cell of metamaterial director has resonance frequency of 1.8 GHz, covering the frequency band of LTE system (1.72 GHz-1.83GHz). By using this technique, the unit cell can have negative permeability, the required property in design at the resonance frequency. It is found that size of the designed interdigital CPW unit cell has been reduced to <tex>$\lambda/8$</tex>. The result causes from the slow wave effect on transmission line in the structure, which electrical and physical lengths of transmission line are not equal from that effect. The unit cell size of 14 mm was designed and used to form a <tex>$7\times 7$</tex> array as a result of metamaterial director with overall size of 98 mm. The 1.8 GHz dipole antenna was then used with the metamaterial director. The results show that the simulation impedance matching result less than −10 dB with the bandwidth of 183 MHz. Using the designed director, the antenna gain has been increased from 2 dB to 5.91 dB with directional radiation pattern. The proposed metamaterial director is appropriate for modern wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) Estimation based on Filter Augmented Imaging
abstract: The Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) is one of the vegetation indices widely used by researchers from different countries for measuring vegetation in inland areas. NDVI measures the greenness of a plant or area by using radiance and reflectivity of light from the sun to calculate the difference between near-infrared (vegetation strongly reflects) and red light (vegetative absorbs). The information derived from NDVI measurement has increased the probability of a good harvest. However, NDVI equipment is relatively expensive causing challenges to accessibility for low-income farmers in developing countries. By using filter-augmented imaging devices, a low-cost camera can be translated to an NDVI sensor. This study discusses the details of filter augmentation, algorithm development, and validation in comparison with a commercially available multispectral camera for NDVI measurements. The filter-augmented imaging device obtained similar results to commercially available NDVI cameras when the target of interest is a vegetative matter such as leaves and grass.

articleTitle: Smart e-Public Bus Station Module via on Cloud-based PLC plus HMI Control System for New Nannal Services
abstract: The paper presents the prototype module of an electronics public bus station system for servicing as the smart public bus system in the new normal scenario. The aim of this paper was proposed the smart public automation module that based on electronics and digital control platform acted as paradigm shift design for approaching to the smart city of Thailand 4.0 policy especially for public transport systems which have a new service paradigm for crowded people in COVID-19 crisis as an endemic situations. The social distancing policy is one of the best way to use in this scenario, while the cloud communicating technology based on the new era of Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) system and Human Machine Interface (HMI) module that can work together for implementing an ordinary PLC with high ability to operate for a long distance communication control with touchless or exposure reduction in the universal prevention scheme and also optimizing the overall performance of the system in the same time. For the renewable energy consumption, the photovoltaic (PV) of solar cell system was used as the solar rooftop of the bus station module with the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) control by Arduino Controller in the battery charging process. The simulations results and many test of real prototype module results in the laboratory scenario were satisfied the V-shaped model analysis concept, but the all of system must be revised again in on-site public area for more practical usage.

articleTitle: A Quasi FSS Reflector with Dualband Cross Dipole for 5G Base Station Antenna Application
abstract: This article describes the application of a quasi-frequency selective surface (FSS) reflector to a cross-dipole antenna for a 5G base station communication system. The quasi-FSS is composed of a square patch resonator with a resonance frequency of 1800 MHz and a perfect electric conductor (PEC) that reflects electromagnetic waves of all frequencies. Moreover, it can support and reflect two linear polarizations (±45°) of a dual-band cross-dipole antenna with dual operating frequencies of 700 MHz and 1800 MHz. At 700 MHz and 1800 MHz, the impedance characteristic of the antenna with reflector is approximately 26.83% and 34.86 % for Sll and S22 ≤-10 dB (±45°). The measured peak gain of the antenna is around 5.74 dBi at 775MHz and 11.88 dBi at 1850MHz. With a quasi-FSS reflector, the proposed antenna can also create a directional radiation pattern and facilitate the utilization of a 5G mobile communication base station.

articleTitle: Power Quality Analysis and Enhancement for Grid Integration of Distributed Energy Resources: Photovoltaic and EV Charging Station using Active Power Filter
abstract: This paper propose the power quality analysis and enhancement for grid-integrated DER: case study of VSPP type photovoltaic and public EV charging station, that effect increase harmonics problem in the distribution grid. Therefore, harmonic voltage compensation process for grid connected-DER and charging station in power system is presented. The integrated method with low-pass filter and active filter are applied, both connected in series with the voltage harmonic detection method. This study using the theory of instantaneous reactive power and hysteresis. In order to study the change in voltage harmonics and to study the efficiency of the harmonic filter circuit. It has been designed using the average %THDv of supply voltage as a benchmark for comparative performance. According to the PEA standard and the system simulation results, it has been found that the designed series active power filter resulted in an average %THDv value are reduced 83.11% after compensation.

articleTitle: Swine Body Temperature Monitoring System
abstract: African Swine Fever is a highly contagious viral infection in swine family. Affecting the economy and the swine farming industry is high and also create an impact to farmers. Because if farmers who raise swine have not plan to prepare for the disease that will occur, it will cause enormous damage. One of the observations of this disease is having a high fever. This is the origin of the system to detect the temperature in swine body. This system will measure the temperature of the swine body. If there is a temperature indicating a high fever, it can alert the farmer to promptly dispose of it.

articleTitle: Thai Fake News Detection Using Machine Learning Model
abstract: Fake news is one of the most critical social issues in the era of modern technology. Fake news detection is the first step in stopping the spread of news widely. This paper proposes detecting fake news using the machine learning models. There are three popular models: Support Vector Machine, Naive Bayes, and Neural Network. The normalization technique is the main step to transform the data to be on a similar dimension before using the machine learning model. For better efficiency and stability of the model training. The results showed that Support Vector Machine achieved an accuracy of 80% than others. And the word list feature has the impact of optimizing the accuracy of the model.

articleTitle: IoT Assisted Oxygen Control Monitoring in Microbial Propagation for Shrimp Ponds
abstract: Oxygen control in microbial propagation for shrimp ponds by monitoring through IoT system the objective is to create and develop an oxygen control system for microbial propagation in shrimp ponds via an IoT system. It is a system that controls the amount of oxygen in the tank of microbial propagation for shrimp ponds by measuring the amount of dissolved oxygen in the water that the sensor can measure, which will be displayed via the Blynk application on a mobile phone. Determination of the performance of oxygen control in microbial propagation for shrimp ponds by monitoring through IoT system and comparing dissolved oxygen measurements in the shrimp pond propagation tank between the laboratory dissolved oxygen meter and an oxygen control system in microbial propagation for shrimp ponds with an IoT system with an oxygen sensor in the water. By checking the dissolved oxygen content in the microbial expansion tank for shrimp ponds every day, three times a day at 9:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m. It will take no more than 72 hours to compare the accuracy of the measuring instrument between the oxygen meter in the water and the oxygen control system in microbial propagation for shrimp ponds using an IoT system with oxygen sensors in the water. When considering the values obtained from the dissolved oxygen measurement test in all periods of testing, the results show that the total dissolved oxygen measured by the oxygen meter was 5.48 mg/l, and the total dissolved oxygen value measured by the oxygen control system in microbial propagation for shrimp ponds using the IoT system was 5.47 mg/l. The dissolved oxygen value measured by the oxygen meter was 0.01 mg/l higher than the dissolved oxygen from the oxygen control system for shrimp aquaculture with IoT systems, representing an average error of 0.2%.

Author Keywords: Oxygen control in microbial propagation for shrimp ponds by monitoring through IoT system

articleTitle: A 0.5 V Modified Pseudo-Differential Current-Starved Ring-VCO with Linearity Improvement for IoT Devices
abstract: Ring-VCO (Voltage controlled oscillator)-based ADCs are suitable for data acquisition in IoT devices due to simple delay elements configuration in the chain. The future development of IoT devices will be directed towards ultra-low operating voltage and reduce their size and area cost. However, the low operating voltage further degrades the linear voltage-to-frequency (V-to-F) tuning characteristics of ring-VCO. The ring-VCO based on complementary bias voltage controls approach achieved the linear V-to-F tuning characteristic at sub-/near threshold operating voltage. The ring-VCO relied on the current-starved pseudo-differential ring-VCO configuration in which a huge number of transistors occupied one delay element. This paper presents the novel current-starved pseudo-differential delay element, which has decreased overhead transistors by 37.5% and sizing by 44.88% compared with the previous work while not adversely affecting the linearity of V-to-F tuning characteristic. Simulation results with a 0.5V operating circuit designed in TSMC <tex>$0.18\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> CMOS technology shows that the maximum nonlinearity error is below 1.3% for 4-stage and phase noise is 95.01dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset frequency.

articleTitle: Reinforced Deep Learning By Discriminant Feature Trace Transform
abstract: Classification of objects using YOLO deep learning is currently very popular. When the discovered object is rotated, however, the pre-trained YOLO model frequently generates incorrect answer predictions. In order to improve the accuracy of the YOLO deep learning pre-trained model, we present in this paper a method for rotating an object's image back to its initial gain using the DFTF algorithm. The DFTF algorithm is designed to take the results of the trace transform and accumulate the values for each column in order to predict the object's degree of rotation. The results of this calculation are then used to rotate the object back to its normal axis. The experiment is therefore a collaboration between YOLO and DFTF with the aim of more accurately predicting the object's responses. Five groups of data will be chosen for experimentation, each of which can be used to determine the precision of the experimental image with rotational issues. The average of accuracy is 98.56%.

articleTitle: A Minimized Thickness of MIMO Antenna Based on Thin Film Substrates for UWB application
abstract: This paper presents a compact MIMO antenna for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications. It is created based on a thin film for an antenna substrate to minimize the antenna thickness, resulting in the antenna being utilized well on a curved surface. The film thickness is about 0.056 mm was used to design and cooperate with the rectangular slot antenna and rectangular stub. In addition, the antenna cover frequency range from 3.1 GHz to 10.6 GHz with the S11 and S21 below −10 dB and −15 dB, respectively. The antenna will be fed by <tex>$50\ \Omega$</tex> coplanar waveguide for a transmission line. Moreover, an Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) isn't more than 0.05 throughout the frequency range. The antenna radiation pattern is bidirectional all bands and the maximum gain is 4.6 dBi. The proposed antenna can be applied to the WBAN WPAN and WLAN, UWB communication systems as well.

articleTitle: Longitudinal Stability Assessment of Fixed-Wing UAV based on Fuzzy Closed-Loop Control
abstract: A fixed-wing UAV may lose its stability due to external disturbances from wind gusts, rainstorms, snow showers, and unpredicted weather conditions. The longitudinal control of the UAV plays an important role in dealing with longitudinal disturbances. This paper proposes adaptive closed-loop controllers based on fuzzy logic together with proportional-integral/derivative (PI/PD) control to attenuate the dynamic effects from disturbances, leading to the improvement of UAV longitudinal stability. The studied system uses a typical UAV model of the Cessna 182 to identify the UAV characteristics with respect to dynamic transfer functions for designing the relevant controllers. The fuzzy rule base is formulated to establish the suitable control gains of PI/PD, resulting in the improvement of dynamic responses in both transient and steady states. The case studies are performed in the MATLAB/Simulink® environment. The obtained results signify that the Fuzzy-PI and Fuzzy-PD controllers could significantly augment the longitudinal stability of the fixed-wing UAV, reducing system overshoots and settling time.

articleTitle: Smart Healthcare device based on IoT
abstract: This work presents the development of a very user-friendly smart healthcare device for people of any age. The device is based on the IoT concept. The hardware was designed around the ESP32 development board, which processes the data acquired from four essential and well-known body sensors (temperature, pulse, oximetry, and EKG). The device can be powered from any 5V DC power supply through the micro-USB port of the ESP32 board. We implemented two operation modes for the device: an “online” one where sensor measurements are sent and stored through WiFi internet connection in a database and an “offline” mode without an internet connection where the measurements are shown only on the LCD. In both operation modes, the instructions are given step by step to the user on the LCD screen. In the case of the “online” mode of operation, we structured a database to store the measured data and represent it eloquently on a public website. We developed an Android app with four user data links to permit quick access to the website. In this manner, the measured data can be accessed by the end user and accredited medical personnel. Thus, doctor and patient interaction would be much tighter for better health control.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study on Effects of Dust Particle Sizes on Efficiency of Monocrystalline Solar Cells
abstract: This study investigates an experimental study on the effect of different types of soil dust particles on efficiency and electric characteristics of the monocrystalline silicon solar cells when tested in an artificial sunlight room with a constant radiation source. It was tested at a constant light intensity of 500 W/m<sup>2</sup> under normal air temperature conditions at 25 °C. The experiment used soil dust from the roads and construction, and five sizes of soil dust particles: <tex>$32-37\ \mu\mathrm{m},\ 38-62\ \mu\mathrm{m},\ 63- 74\ \mu\mathrm{m},\ 75-89\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> and <tex>$90-105\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> in amounts ranging from 1 - 5 g. The experimental results showed that the accumulated of soil dust on the surface of the solar cell panel, <tex>$32-37\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> (fine particles) thicknesses and amounts ranging from 1 - 5 g, reduced the solar cell panel electric power generated by 7.30 - 19.79% and was the maximum efficiency loss. The soil dust size is <tex>$90 - 105\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> (coarse particles) thicknesses, the largest size for this study, reduced the solar cell panel electric power generated by 2.23 - 9.59% and was to be the minimum performance loss. In this study, fine soil dust particles had a more significant impact on efficiency reduction for the solar cell panel compared to soil dust coarse particles.

articleTitle: A Study of Paddy Moisture Content Determination with Reflected wave
abstract: This work purposed to study on paddy moisture content measurement with microwave technique that reflected wave were analyzed. The free space method was selected by using an antenna and network analyzer for measuring reflected wave from paddy sample. The experiment results are clearly about the different S<inf>11</inf> and various moisture contents at frequency range 0.8 - 3 GHz. It is possible to design a simple paddy moisture content determination tool by choosing suitable frequency from experiment results.

articleTitle: A Centralized System for Detecting Attacks from Windows Event Logs
abstract: Although Microsoft released Windows 10 and 11, many personal computers worldwide are still running the old Windows 7 version without installing security patches. This leads attackers to be able to exploit them. In this paper, we propose a lightweight system called SHIRO to detect Windows attacks from the Windows event logs. It aims to detect attacks on Windows 7 clients by focusing on three most critical Common Vulnerabilities Exposures (CVEs), which are CVE 2017–0143 (EternalBlue), CVE 2017–0199 (HTA), and CVE 2019–0708 (BlueKeep). To validate our proposed system, we emulate various attacks and generate datasets on each attack type. Then the log server collects Windows event logs from each client. We identify attacks by comparing logs obtained during attacks and logs obtained during normal operations. Then we develop detection signatures for each CVE from specific event IDs. Once SHIRO finds the attack signatures in the records, it identifies the attack type and alerts to the administrator. Our experiments based on both pre-generated datasets and the real-time attacks confirm that SHIRO can detect three types of attacks accurately. The experiment results prove that SHIRO is useful for the administrator to find the compromised Windows machines efficiently.

articleTitle: Simulation and Evaluation of Solid-State Fault Current Limiter in Electric Distribution System
abstract: The widespread use of electric loads and natural disasters are the major causes of power quality problems. For instance, the high fault current level leads to electricity interruption and outages. Thus, pruning fault current down to the optimum level is the proper method for power quality improvement. This paper presents a comprehensive performance evaluation using solid-state fault current limiters (SSFCLs) in a distribution system. The proposed SSFCL simulation consists of EMTP modeling and coding by GNU Octave. Fault detection is the essential mechanism that applies the p-q theory. With the proposed SSFCL, the simulation results were shown the performance of fast fault detection and fault current limitation. The simulation results with <tex>$LC$</tex> loads show that the proposed SSFCL effectively limits fault currents. Moreover, it can protect the outage and voltage sag at the point of common coupling (PCC) subjected to various types of faults.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Wind Speed Measurement from Meteorological Mast and LiDAR
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of wind speed measured using cup anemometers installed on meteorological mast and LiDAR. The measurement site is in north-eastern area of Thailand named Nawang in Khemmarat district of Ubonratchathani. In this study, data collection over a month is examined. To verify that the wind speed obtained from LiDAR can replace that from cup anemometers, a number of statistical analyses are applied. The results show some similar and different features between the two groups of data.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of Peanut Harvesting Machine based Dual Spiral Coupling Electric Motor Drives
abstract: This paper proposes a peanut harvesting machine based on dual spiral coupling an electric motor drives and its performance when compared to the human harvesting. The proposed machine had function to pick up the peanut pods from their stems by using dual special coupling mechanical part driven by just a single-phase electric motor. The test results showed that the proposed machine could harvest the peanuts with the average productivity of 258 pods per minute or 15,480 pods per hour at its nominal speed, which was approximately 2.7 times faster than the human.

articleTitle: Improvement of Power Oscillation Damping by Using a Unified Power Flow Controller: Case Study of NamTheun 2 Transmission Line
abstract: The electrical power system is growing fastly and becoming more complex. The increase in load demand in power transmission line systems can have a significant impact on stability and reliability. This paper presents the stability improvement of 500 kV transmission line systems using a Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC) for power oscillation damping. The transmission line between Nam Theun 2 (Laos) and Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT) grid connection has been selected as a case study model. The simulation model takes into account the three-phase faults and sudden load decreasing/increasing. The simulation has been conducted using MATLAB/Simulink by assuming a power system network with and without the UPFC. The results illustrate the ability of the system with UPFC to deal with the fault.

articleTitle: An Investigation on Multi-step Bitcoin Prediction based on LSTM and GRU
abstract: This work aims to conduct an investigation on 2-, 5- and 10 –output-step with 5 fixed input-step Bitcoin price prediction, using gated recurrent unit (GRU) and long short-term memory (LSTM). The effects of using 2 and 6 layers with regard to LSTM and GRU (2L- and 6L- LSTM and GRU) on the prediction performance are also examined. Two datasets with statistically distinct features, e.g., rather monotonic and non-monotonic, consecutively referred to Binance and Poloniex, the world's leading crypto trading and cryptocurrency exchange platforms are experimented for intensifying the investigation. Prediction performance evaluations include root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) along with Pearson correlation coefficient (Corr) are employed here. The best averaged results of all the measures are generated by 2L-GRU. 0.9873, 0.9777 and 0.9593 Corr means are generated by 2-, 5- and 10- output-step; and 0.9758, 0.9575 and 0.9259 Corr means are resulted by the same numbers of steps, respectively for Binance and Poloniex. Overall prediction performance based on more-simpler, monotonic Binance data is rather better than more – complicate, non-monotonic Poloniex data.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a FIX Protocol Offload Engine for SET Market Data
abstract: This paper presents the design of a FIX protocol offload engine for SET market data processing. To achieve low latency, parallel and pipelining concepts are utilized wherever possible. Our design is implemented through VHDL code on an Intel MAX10 board at 125-MHz based clock with 1 GbE network. The results show that the Rx module can achieve a maximum decoding latency of <tex>$4.032\ \mu\mathrm{s}$</tex> and a constant processing delay of 26 clock cycles after a FIX market data was received while the Tx module achieves a maximum latency of <tex>$3.98\ \mu\mathrm{s}$</tex> for generating a FIX market data request. Moreover, the <tex>$T$</tex> x/Rx module has an ability to encode/decode 8-digit ASCII values. The latency of the design can be further improved using a higher data width or greater gigabit ethernet environment.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Contingency Analysis Considering Renewable Energy Introduction in the Case of Power Generation Outage
abstract: In the case of using fluctuating renewable energy as a spinning reserve when a power supply unit is disconnected, this reserve power cannot be frequency-adjusted and can be operated in combination with other regulated power sources. Therefore, safe operation is necessary to avoid fluctuations. In particular, the power flow in a transmission line should not exceed the upper limit of its operational capacity. In this work, assuming that a certain amount of power supply failure can occur, we aimed to obtain the probability distribution of the transmission line power as the cause of fluctuating renewable energy and the cumulative distribution function of transmission line capacity. From the evaluation of the several case studies based on published system information, it was found that even a variable power supply can be used as a reserve power against power supply failures by utilizing revere line power flows. Moreover, we found that the supply and demand balance can be ensured to avoid the transmission line overloads considering the regulated power supply's location and the injection of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Material Volume Estimation in Cylindrical Silo Using Acoustic Impulse and Broadband Excitations
abstract: This work presents a study of estimating material volumes in an oblique cylindrical silo using acoustic impulses and broadband waves. Silo as an acoustical, linear and time-invariant system was assumed and frequency response of the system can be determined. Three types of system excitations, acoustic impulses, white and pink noises were used. The acoustic impulses were generated from a silo-knocking mechanism, controlled by a microcontroller and computer. White and pink noises were generated using computer programming and fed to a loudspeaker in the silo via a sound interface and power amplifier. Acoustic waves in the silo were gathered by a microphone and digitally processed for extracting the silo's frequency responses in frequency domain. The resonance frequencies and corresponding mode numbers were used to calculate a length of air cavities in the cylindrical silo. With known dimension of the silo, volumes of remaining materials can be obtained. Experimentations were done to estimate volumes of cement, sand, and water in a laboratory-sized cylindrical silo. Results showed that the acoustic impulse excitation only yielded volume estimates for certain volume levels and their estimation errors were quite high. Material volume estimations obtained by using white and pink noise excitation yielded very satisfactory accuracy. Averaged error percentages for estimations of cement, sand, and water volume were 0.67%, 1.27% and 1.05% when the white noise was used, and 1.31%, 1.13% and 1.64% when the pink noise was utilized, respectively.

articleTitle: Firearm Training System by Laser gun
abstract: This research presents a combat system with weapons, laser guns and electronic armor. Practicing firearms tactics results in shooting and maneuvering skills. The system consists of a laser gun that can determine the amount of ammunition used. The target of the armor has a sensor that receives laser light emitted by the gun. The guns and targets are controlled via a wireless network with a Node Micro Controller Unit (NodeMCU) connected to broker and can be displayed via computers, mobile phones and tablets. The IoT system uses protocol MQTT, the system used to store data on both sides of the device for response to the loss of network connection. The training is a gun fight between two players. The training is gun fighting between two players shooting guns against each other. The referee, commander and the audience can track the score of both players in real time. The training is safe to reduce the accidents of the practice also reduces the cost of training and can be practiced both indoors and outdoors.

articleTitle: Electromechanical behavior of red blood cells in insulator-based dielectrophoretic device
abstract: We investigated the dielectrophoresis (DEP) of red blood cells by observing the critical frequencies that cause the cells to change between positive DEP to negative DEP. We fabricated a microfluidic device composed of a microchannel and electrodes. Red blood cells suspended in a conductive buffer were fed into the device and the DEP experiment was performed to determine the critical frequency of the red blood cells. Subsequently, the experimental critical frequencies were used to calculate electrical parameters, cytoplasmic conductivity and membrane capacitance, of the cells.

articleTitle: Improvement Impedance Bandwidth of Printed Dipole Antenna for Digital television Applications
abstract: Improvement Bandwidth Impedance of Dipole Antenna for Digital Television Applications presented in this. It is designed at a lower frequency center frequency and higher frequency of 510, 650 and 790 MHz, respectively. By using end each line has the circled radial (R1) sent more effect to impedance matching, the proposed antenna be able to responds to peculiarly wide impedance bandwidth to 470 - 862 MHz covering the operation frequencies of DTV systems. Furthermore, this paper proposed concept offers the benefit of a wider and matching impedance of the bandwidth, while also progressive the gain equal to 1.83, 2.35, 2.51 dB up to 6.11, 5.81, 6.02 dB, respectively. When the compared to a basic printed dipole. Other than, the spurious proposed printed dipole antenna has a good agreement between simulated and the measured, which confirms the broadband behavior for DTV reception application.

articleTitle: Improved Partial Retransmission Hard-Decision Message-Passing ARQ
abstract: The proposed improvement on hard-decision message-passing (hMP-ARQ) method can verify correct symbols when there is a group of common error symbols in a pair of check nodes. This leads to a better performance than the existing hMP-ARQ. At symbol error probability (Ps) of 0.2, the average numbers of frames for successful transmission were reduced to only 42% and 46% of the existing hMP-ARQ for (45,30) and (60,30) codes respectively. With lower complexity, it even performs better than block Vector Symbol Decoding ARQ (BVSD-ARQ) for a (60,30) LDPC code and Ps < 0.175. Thus, it is a good choice for partial retransmission ARQ.

articleTitle: Passive Radio Localization System Using Channel Impulse Response and Deep Learning
abstract: Device-free passive indoor localization is playing a crucial role in some applications like smart homes and intrusion detection. While most systems are designed to locate humans, this research demonstrates that it is possible to use a device-free passive technique to locate a small object in a Non Line Of Sight (NLOS) indoor environment using only one antenna acting as an emitter and another as a receiver. i.e., a single radio frequency (RF) link. The fingerprinting technique is used. The channel impulse response (CIR) is used as a signature, it is obtained by the IFFT of the channel frequency response. Signatures are matched to positions using machine learning (ML) techniques. The results show that it is possible to accurately locate an object of a few centimetres with good accuracy.

articleTitle: How many appropriate added synthetic data to improve semantic segmentation?
abstract: Nowadays, autonomous vehicle technology plays a more important role in our lives. Many people pay attention to driverless cars, but, in fact, every industry needs technology that increases safety. But the problem is that the data must be diverse. We proposed a data synthesis in which the number of the two sources needed to be a reasonable ratio. In this paper, the ratio between synthetic and real data is observed experimentally with clearly and noise injection data in the Yolact and Detectron2 model. In the benchmark test, the optimal ratio is 3.5 and 2.5 for Yolact and Detectron2, respectively. Moreover, provided that training data with mixing data method provide better accuracy than one data type training method.

articleTitle: A Classifiers Experimentation with Quantum Machine Learning
abstract: Quantum Computing is a new way to create a different type of computer system from Quantum Mechanics. Quantum machine learning is one of the applications took the benefit from qauntum computers. In this experiment, we use the IBM Qiskit library to study how well a quantum machine learning classifier works. We made two different colored dots to represent the two-class dataset. The quantum circuit can be collected from the Qiskit library. The 1<sup>st</sup> and 2<sup>nd</sup> order feature map schemes operated by oracle quantum oracle functions are applied before making a classification. Finally, we can call the quantum support vector machine or QSVM function to classify data. Kernel matrix from the studied qauntum model shows that quantum computing can be used to clearly classify classes of the dataset with 100 percent accuracy.

articleTitle: Low Complexity Nonbinary Decoder: Correct Only Data part with Implementation
abstract: For systematic nonbinary codes, there is no need to correct erroneous parity check symbols since users need only the decoded data symbols. This idea can be generally applied for systematic nonbinary codes.
